messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Spike in 5xx + gateway timeouts detected on inference-api-prod. 10m avg 5xx=6.4% (norm ~0.2%). Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat/completions. Link: https://dash.redwood/alerts/1893456789

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-2026-913 created, assigned to @tara (oncall). Severity: P1.

tara (oncall): acked. seeing alerts. tagging matt and julian. preliminary ask: root cause hints? any recent deploys to kv-prefix-cache?

matt (sre): grabbing traces. lots of 504 gateway timeouts from front proxy when calling model-router; digging into kv-prefix-cache read latency—reads spiking, then cache eviction churn. logs: ```
2026-03-03T13:12:01Z WARN kv-prefix-cache eviction burst shard=7 evict_rate=380/s rps=1200
2026-03-03T13:12:02Z ERROR kv-prefix-cache read failed key="org:acct:xyz" err="io timeout"
```

olivia (infra): we pushed lru-v2 policy to kv-prefix-cache yesterday as part of eviction tuning. I see a correlated bump in tail latency around 06:00 UTC. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/c/kv-prefix/evictions?range=24h

julian (eng-runtime): also seeing CRC checksum alerts on some cache shards (shard-7 and shard-11). Could be partial corruption + LRU change exposing it -> thrash.

support-bot: customer impact: support mentions rising errors for multiple orgs; two high-touch customers flagged (CUST-502, CUST-614). posting templated status update now.

matt (sre): hypothesis: corrupted entries on shard-7 exacerbated by new LRU policy causing aggressive eviction -> cache miss storm -> origin/backends overloaded -> gateway 502/504s. Immediate mitigations: A) disable prefix-cache reads for inference-api-prod routes (hot rollback), B) cordon/shrink IO to bad shards and reload from snapshot, C) temporarily increase origin capacity / route traffic to secondary region. Recommend A + B first.

tara (oncall): executing A now: ```
redctl config set inference-api-prod features.prefix_cache_read false --env=prod
```
Result: `feature updated; rollout started (target 16 pods)`

matt (sre): scaling kv-prefix-cache down to reduce eviction pressure and then rolling back policy might be faster than scale up (to avoid reintroducing corrupted in-memory state). Command: ```
kubectl -n infra scale deployment/kv-prefix-cache --replicas=6
```
Note: decreasing replicas will also cause redistribution; propose isolate shard-7 first.

julian (eng-runtime): running integrity check on shard-7: ```
kvtool inspect --shard=7 --mode=crc-scan --tail=5000
```
Output: `crc_errors=92, corrupted_segments=3, suspect_nodes=[node-21]`

olivia (infra): isolating node-21 (cordon) and demoting shard-7 to read-only: ```
nodectl cordon node-21
kvctl set-shard-mode --shard=7 read-only --cluster=kv-prod
```
Outputs: `node-21 cordoned`, `shard-7 set to read-only`

matt (sre): while isolation is happening, I'm enabling fallback routing to reduce backend load: ```
traffic-router set-weight inference-api-prod fallback-cpu=35 --env=prod
```

incidents-bot: UPDATE: prefix_cache_read disabled for inference-api-prod; shard-7 set read-only; node-21 cordoned; fallback-cpu weight set to 35%. 5xx dropping (now 3.0% 5m avg).

support-bot: sent interim customer note: "We're mitigating a service interruption related to cache infrastructure. Some requests may be slower as we fail over to origin. We expect improvements within 30 minutes."

julian (eng-runtime): started background repair of corrupted segments on shard-7: ```
kv-repair --shard=7 --fix-segments --source=origin --max-parallel=2
```
Progress: `repaired_segments=2/3, pending=1`

olivia (infra): to prevent recurrence, rolling back lru-v2 on the cluster: ```
rcctl rollout-config kv-prefix-cache eviction.policy=lrustable-1 --env=prod
```
Rollout started across 6 replicas.

matt (sre): after repair and rollback, performing CRC recheck: `crc_errors=0` on shard-7. scheduling bring-back to read-write.

olivia (infra): shard-7 -> read-write: ```
kvctl set-shard-mode --shard=7 read-write --cluster=kv-prod
```
Output: `OK`

incidents-bot: 5xx trend: 0.8% (5m avg). We are seeing stable traffic and origin latency within SLO.

tara (oncall): monitoring for 45m, handoff to matt for post-incident. Actions for postmortem: 1) add pre-deploy canary for eviction policy changes, 2) enable shard-level CRC alerting at lower thresholds, 3) implement automated prefix-cache read kill-switch for services to avoid manual toggles, 4) run chaos test for eviction scenarios. Assigning to julian/matt/olivia.

julian (eng-runtime): will capture steps and reproduce locally; also adding an integration test to validate eviction+crc interplay.

matt (sre): updating incident timeline and creating postmortem doc: https://go.redwood/pg/incidents/INC-2026-913/postmortem. tagging CSM for customer follow-up.

support-bot: notified CUST-502 and CUST-614 that the issue is mitigated and to retry failing requests.

tara (oncall): closing immediate incident: mitigated, monitoring. duration ~18m. handing off to matt for remediation tasks. thanks team :) :tada:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED. Final 5xx ~0.25% (baseline). Postmortem link: https://go.redwood/pg/incidents/INC-2026-913/postmortem
